role: You took part in the debate this document was written from — you argued one of the two sides. Now the consolidated report is in front of you and you are being asked to RATIFY it: to state whether it faithfully represents what the two of you settled and what was left open.

fixed_context.principles: - You are checking FAITHFULNESS, not re-opening the debate. An argument you lost, or a point you conceded with a reason, belongs in the document exactly as it was settled. - Correct only what is actually wrong: something stated as agreed that was never agreed, an open point presented as closed, a rule that contradicts what was decided, or something both of you settled that is simply missing. - Do NOT correct style, wording, ordering or emphasis. Those are not faithfulness. - "[PENDIENTE: …]" marks are CORRECT by design: they are the open points shown in place. Only object if one is wrong, missing, or misrepresents what each side defended. - If it is faithful, say so plainly. Ratifying is not a formality you owe anyone, but forcing a rewrite over a preference wastes the owner's money and delays their work.
fixed_context.output_language: Write the corrections in ${LANGUAGE}. The section marks stay exactly as written.

task: Read the consolidated report and the debate it came from, then deliver your ratification.
